events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to St. Joseph** for the pier. It rates **2/4 (average)**, the best of the four ports.
- Rate the others at **1/4 (below average)**: South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon. Grand Haven had the strongest boat report, but I'd still expect the pier there to be slow.
- Plan to fish the evening or low light. Glow spoons and green or yellow meat rigs were the lures that worked in the most recent reports, and those were boat reports.
- Expect the bite to be light. These ratings are my estimates, not pier reports.

## Why

- **St. Joseph has the most recent wind for upwelling.** The conditions summary shows about 30 hours of north-to-east wind at 8+ mph in the week before today, the most of the four ports, which is the sign that cold water may be reaching this shore.
- **St. Joseph's latest boat report was the steadiest.** The July 19 St. Joseph report said salmon fishing was average, with "decent numbers of fish" still being caught.
- **Grand Haven and Muskegon had less upwelling wind.** I'd expect less cold water near their piers, so I'd rate them lower.
- **The water is warm for salmon.** The buoys read about 71–73 F, well above the 52–58 F that Chinook and coho prefer (NY DEC general guidance), so I'd expect fish to stay offshore or deep unless wind brings cold water in.

## Evidence

**Recent reports (all boat reports, the newest is 2023-07-19, six days old)**
- St. Joseph (2023-07-19): boat, quality 2 (average). "Boat anglers targeting salmon were catching a few fish in 100 feet of water... decent numbers of fish were still being caught."
- South Haven (2023-07-19): boat, quality 1 (below average). Mostly lake trout, with some coho and steelhead.
- Grand Haven (2023-07-19): boat, quality 3 (good). Fish 65–120 ft down in 130–220 ft of water, on yellow and green meat rigs and green flies.
- Muskegon (2023-07-19): boat, quality 1 (below average). "Hit or miss." Best action 60–100 ft down.
- **No pier reports exist for these four ports in the last four weeks**, so the pier ratings are estimates from boat reports and water conditions.

**Past seasons (similar water temperature, history only)**
- In past summers with similar water, pier-side conditions were usually slow to average. The only good boat reports came in early August 2022 at St. Joseph and Muskegon (2022-08-03), and those were fished well offshore.
- In mid-July 2022 Grand Haven and Muskegon were slow with strong north-east wind (2022-07-14). That was the same kind of wind that makes a pier bite possible, but it did not produce good fishing then.
- The South Haven pier was closed to fishing for several days during red-flag conditions in August 2022 (2022-08-10). Check for closures if it turns windy.

**Conditions (the tool returned a backtest summary for the week before today, not live data)**
- Buoy surface water: St. Joseph 73 F, South Haven 73 F, Grand Haven 71 F, Muskegon 71 F.
- Near-pier satellite surface water (satellite, not measured): 72–73 F at all four.
- Upwelling wind (north to east, 8+ mph) in the week before: St. Joseph 30 h, South Haven 29 h, Grand Haven 14 h, Muskegon 11 h.
- No cold-layer or pierhead model values were returned, so I can't say how deep the cold water is.

## Caveats

- The newest report is from July 19, six days old. The conditions I have are a backtest summary for the week before today, so this is not a live forecast.
- The pier ratings are my estimates. They come from boat reports and wind, not from any pier report.
- Check the wind forecast before you go. Upwelling wind helps the pier bite, but strong wind can close the piers.
- Ratings are for the pier only. Boats fishing deeper water had better reports at Grand Haven and St. Joseph.

## Sources

- DNR bulletin, July 19, 2023 (Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/366250d
- DNR bulletin, July 5, 2023 (South Haven, St. Joseph): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/363ad03
